Great food! Authentic decor!
Mar 2018 • Business
Highway4 is close to Daewoo Hotel. Just around 5 minutes walk from the Hotel. I was seated on the ground floor. The tiled table and the plants in the restaurant add a lot of flavor. I ordered:

~ Highway4 rice paper roll: fried fish fillet (with mayo inside) in the rice paper with special dipping sauce. The sauce has wasabi, interesting! But even without dipping the special sauce, the rice paper roll is still yummy!

~Pan fried coconut heart with garlic: the thin sliced coconut heart looks like bamboo shoot, yet, much crunchier. Very good!

~ baby clams with minced pork and rice cake: the portuon is big! A little bit spicy but the smells and tastes very good!

~ Iced corn tea: soothing!

Not for me
Jan 2018
We went to Highway4 as it was one of the few non Japanese restaurants close to our hotel. We walked right past it and then found it as we walked back again . 
We got a table on the 3rd floor. The stairway is badly lit and at this time of year the room was cold so I kept my jacket on. 
We ordered crab spring rolls and pork spring rolls , pork steak and beef shank. The English descriptions are a bit deceiving as everything was different to what we expected. The pork dish came first and the cubed pork was quite tough. The beef arrived when we finished the pork. We were so disappointed it was cold thin cuts of beef. After we got through it the spring rolls arrived and they were quite tasty and hot . 
All this including 2 Coca Colas came to 459000 which is just under £15 
It wasn’t a comfortable place to be or to sit. Too dark and dingy and no atmosphere

Highway4 is a very famous chain Vietnamese restaurant in Hanoi that you should visit for alternative local Vietnamese dishes and extraordinary liquors. With a perfect location, you can enjoy your dining while sitting at the terrace upstairs seeing a view of Hanoi city.

All that glitters is not gold...
Apr 2017 • Solo
I was walking through narrow winding streets when I came across this gem. From the outside it looks like a prime gorgeous spot to eat at. Overlooking the lake and close to Lotte centre. Charming features, decor with beautiful artistic items on the walls. Some of the tables are even made from doors. And I also love the cushion covers on the chairs. 

What I received was slow and bad service especially considering I was one of the only two customers when I walked in just before lunch. Then people started coming in. I decided to go upstairs to sit there and was asked if I've made a reservation even though there were so many empty spaces. Maybe it was a case of lost in translation but I did not wait for someone to intervene. I went back downstairs to wait for my food...

I was given the menu earlier before attempting to sit upstairs. I browsed through. Waited. Waited. Waited for someone to even look my way. I have been walking and exploring Hanoi in the heat and had no energy to find another restaurant. Finally I had to flag my waiter, Chinh who dumped me with a menu a while ago to take my order. He was snacking on a pineapple and I had to wait for him to finish eating before taking my order.

I ordered spicy satay grilled frog legs (for 130k dong) to try them out. Unfortunately they were dry, with a bland taste, not spicy and no seasoning. Just old cardboard taste and nothing to write home about. Oh but I loved the fresh crispy refreshing Banana flower salad with roasted peanuts (for 60K Dong). Yummy yummy.

After eating I then sat with dishes on the table for over 20 minutes as I wrote this. Even though they were serving the table next to me. I was hoping to get some dessert. But I guess not...

The only highlight was the salad, the music playing. They played two of my favourite, The Script and Micheal Bubble
